model.name: Blue Archive-like Charge
model.blurb: Both banners have a 0.7% pickup rate. At 100 points, you get a 3-star with a 50% pickup chance; at 200, the pickup is guaranteed. A pickup resets the meter, and same-type banners share points.
model.source: Based on Blue Archive JP 5.5 Recruitment Charge (29 July 2026) and the Wiki/Yostar/Inven write-up: at 100 charge, a 3-star is guaranteed with a 50% pickup chance; at 200, the pickup is guaranteed. A pickup on this banner resets charge. Regular and limited banners use separate pools, and banners of the same type share charge. This model does not copy a live drop table.
notes: Every pull adds charge. An off-banner 3-star does not reset it. Any pickup on this banner does, including a natural 0.7% hit.
When charge reaches 100, the roll is a 3-star with a 50% chance of the pickup. If you miss, the next 3-star is not guaranteed to be the pickup.
At 200 charge, the pickup is guaranteed and the meter resets to 0.
Regular and limited banners have separate meters. Banners of the same type share one, so getting A resets the progress you had toward B.

The 5.5 livestream announced the change a few days before it launched in JP. Producer Kim Yong-ha apologised, and recent Steam reviews fell to 'Overwhelmingly Negative.' Those write-ups did not announce a Global release date.

overview.summary: Blue Archive combines tactical team building with a large cast of recruitable students and character stories. This example studies the July 2026 Japanese Recruitment Charge shape already documented in this project. Its progress bar gives rewards at intermediate and final checkpoints, making the next milestone part of the recruitment experience.
overview.distinctive: At charge 100 the example gives a 3-star reward with a 50% featured chance; at 200 it guarantees the featured student. Getting a featured student resets charge, so an early success changes the route to the next one. This differs from accumulated exchange points that survive a lucky pull.
overview.strength: An intermediate checkpoint gives a visible moment of progress before the final guarantee. The design interpretation is that it can make a long chase easier to follow, although losing progress after success may matter to players collecting several students.
overview.analysis: Compare it with the spark example: who gets a first student early, who has to restart, and how long it takes to collect two featured students. Use the project source notes for the dated rule scope.
overview.popularity: Nexon identified Blue Archive as a contributor to stronger-than-expected Q1 2024 revenue. That historical result predates this charge example and cannot establish reception of the July 2026 rule. No player-sentiment or spending study for this exact charge configuration is attached.
overview.business: The recruitment currency can connect character demand to paid top-ups. A checkpoint system changes when players may feel close to a reward, but whether its resets improve or harm spending is a design question to test, not an established profit claim.
